'''Walter John Tomasch''' (July 26, 1930 – October 16, 2026) was an American physicist.

== Early life and career ==
Tomasch was born in [[Cleveland, Ohio]], on July 26, 1930, the son of Julius Tomasch and Helen Schmiedl.<ref name="a">{{Cite web|url=https://www.legacy.com/us/obituaries/name/walter-tomasch-obituary?id=62785039|title=Walter John Tomasch|work=Legacy|access-date=November 2, 2026|via=[[Legacy.com]]}}</ref> He earned his [[Bachelor of Science|BS degree]] at [[Case Western Reserve University]] in 1952. He also earned [[Master of Science|MS degree]] at [[Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute]] in 1955, and earned his [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD degree]] at Case Western in 1958.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://archives.nd.edu/ndr/NDR-35/NDR-2005-06.pdf|title=Walter J. Tomasch|work=[[University of Notre Dame]]|access-date=November 2, 2026}}</ref>

He served as a professor in the department of [[physics]] at the [[University of Notre Dame]]. During his years as a professor, in 1968, he was named a [[Lists of fellows of the American Physical Society|fellow]] of the [[American Physical Society]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/funding-recognition/aps-fellowship?q=tomasch&af=true|title=APS Fellow Archive|work=[[American Physical Society]]|access-date=November 2, 2026}}</ref>

== Personal life and death ==
In 1955, Tomasch married Joyce Ellen Hutyera. They had two children. Their marriage lasted until her death in 2000.<ref name="a" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://ingenweb.org/instjoseph/obits/t/tomaschjoycee.htm|title=Joyce E. Tomasch|work=Ingenweb.org|date=February 26, 2000|access-date=November 2, 2026|first=Mary Jo|last=Koran}}</ref>

Tomasch died at his home on October 16, 2026, at the age of 96.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.palmerfuneralhomes.com/obituary/Walter-Tomasch|title=Walter John Tomasch|work=Palmer Funeral Homes|access-date=November 2, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.echovita.com/us/obituaries/in/south-bend/walter-tomasch-22280656|title=Walter Tomasch|work=Echovita|access-date=November 2, 2026}}</ref>
